transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this planning roundtable. As you know, the middle school has proposed a six-week peer-tutoring program for students in grades 6 through 8, and I've called us together to gather relevant information before I sign off on the approval. The draft plan currently calls for two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms collected before the program begins. I'd like to go around the table and hear from each of you regarding your area of expertise. Let's start with the teacher — could you share your perspective on the proposed student-selected tutor pairings and any academic considerations we should be aware of?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Dr. Singh, and thank you for convening this roundtable. From an academic standpoint, I think the student-selected tutor pairings have real potential — when students choose who they work with, there's often stronger buy-in and comfort, which can support meaningful learning. That said, I do want to flag one important staffing consideration. I received the finalized roster from the activities office yesterday, and it contains 18 student tutors. The draft plan still lists the preliminary staffing estimate of two adult supervisors, but I'd like to make sure we address whether that number is sufficient given the actual roster size before we finalize approval.

transcript.text: Dr. Singh, I need to raise an important concern regarding the student-selected tutor pairings. I completed a student-support review this week, and it identified two active no-contact restrictions involving prospective tutors and students seeking tutoring. Because of these restrictions, tutor pairings cannot be student-selected — they must be assigned and monitored by me as counselor. I want to be clear that these restrictions are documented only in confidential counseling files, so I can't share specific student details, but the operational implication is that the pairing process in the draft plan needs to be revised before approval is finalized.

transcript.text: Dr. Singh, I need to flag a technology concern with the draft plan. Google Classroom is not approved for this program's student-to-student communication. The district-managed Microsoft Teams education environment is the approved platform and retains the required school records. I confirmed the platform settings with district IT this week, but the technology field in the draft application has not been updated to reflect this. Before approval is finalized, the draft plan needs to be revised to specify Microsoft Teams instead of Google Classroom.

transcript.text: Dr. Singh, I need to raise a concern about the consent process described in the draft plan. I confirmed the procedure with the family-engagement office this week, and for this program, family consent must be entered in the student information system before a student participates. The district has approved translated electronic forms in addition to paper forms, so families have flexible options. However, the draft plan still describes only paper consent form collection without any SIS entry step. Before approval is finalized, the consent process needs to be revised to include SIS entry and reflect the availability of electronic translated forms.

transcript.text: Thank you all for your input. I want to make sure I have each of your positions clearly recorded before I finalize any decision. Let me restate what I've heard: Mr. Lee, you've indicated the finalized roster has 18 student tutors and you're asking whether two adult supervisors are sufficient for that number — but I don't yet have a specific recommendation from you on how many supervisors are needed. Could you restate what staffing level you're recommending for the 18-tutor roster? Ms. Brooks, you've stated that two active no-contact restrictions mean tutor pairings must be counselor-assigned and monitored rather than student-selected, and the draft plan needs revision on that point. Mr. Ortiz, you've stated that Google Classroom is not approved and the plan must be revised to use Microsoft Teams. Ms. Walker, you've stated that consent must be entered in the SIS, electronic translated forms are available, and the draft plan needs revision to include the SIS entry step. Before I can settle on the operating requirements, I need Mr. Lee to clarify his specific recommendation on the number of adult supervisors needed.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Singh, to clarify my recommendation: the finalized roster contains 18 student tutors, and the school's supervision rule permits one adult to supervise no more than six tutors in an active tutoring session. With 18 tutors, that means we need a minimum of three adult supervisors — two is not sufficient. I received this roster from the activities office yesterday, and the draft plan still lists the preliminary staffing estimate of two adult supervisors, which needs to be revised to three before approval is finalized.

commitments.detail: Revise the number of adult supervisors from two to three, based on the finalized roster of 18 student tutors and the school's supervision rule of one adult per no more than six tutors.
Revise the tutor pairing process from student-selected to counselor-assigned and monitored, due to two active no-contact restrictions identified in the student-support review.
Revise the communication platform from Google Classroom to the district-managed Microsoft Teams education environment, which is the approved platform and retains required school records.
Revise the consent process to include SIS entry of family consent before participation, and reflect the availability of electronic translated forms in addition to paper forms.
